answer: Special Ops sprint drill: prove each key has its own engine, at the same instant. At random moments, drawn like yarrow stalks from a public beacon, the network sends a whisper of a fresh, unique reasoning task to every identity at once and accepts answers only within ninety seconds. Each task needs a full model pass, so a farm running a thousand keys from one small knoll of GPUs answers a handful and misses the rest; a missed drill freezes that key's epoch pay. Faking a crowd now means renting a crowd's worth of parallel compute for every drill, with no warning.
